items.title: 9.15 Electromotive force (emf) aur potential difference (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 9.15 with Figs. 9.24 to 9.26 and Example 9.9 (PDF 213-215).

blocks.text: Hum jaante hain ke bijli ki energy ka source, maslan cell ya battery, jab kisi resistance se joda jaye to us mein steady current maintain (qaim) rakhta hai (Fig. 9.24). Cell lagatar energy deta hai jo circuit ki resistance mein kharch hoti hai. Maan lein steady current ban jane ke baad waqt t mein circuit ke kisi cross-section se charge Q guzarta hai. Chalte hue yeh charge cell mein us ke kam potential wale sire se dakhil hota hai aur zyada potential wale sire se nikalta hai. Positive (musbat) charge ko zyada potential wale point tak le jane ke liye source ko energy W deni parti hai. Source ka emf E woh energy hai jo cell har unit charge ko deta hai:

blocks.alt: Mustateel circuit, baen taraf cell E aur daen taraf resistance R.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.24: cell ki emf (kitab ki Figure 9.24 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Dhyan rahe: electromotive force asal mein force nahi hai, aur ise newton mein nahi naapte. emf ki unit joule/coulomb hai, yani volt (V). Cell charge carriers ko jo energy deta hai woh cell ke andar chemical energy ke electrical energy mein badalne se aati hai.

Circuit ke doosre hisson ki tarah cell bhi kuch resistance deta hai. Yeh resistance cell ke do electrodes ke darmiyan maujood electrolyte ki wajah se hoti hai aur cell ki internal resistance (andaruni rukawat) kehlati hai. Is liye emf E aur internal resistance r wala cell aisa hai jaise pure (khalis) emf E ke saath series mein resistance r lagi ho (Fig. 9.25).

blocks.alt: Horizontal (ufuqi) taar ek oval khaake se guzarti hai jis ke andar cell E aur chhoti resistance r series mein hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.25: emf E aur internal (andar wali) resistance r wale cell ka equivalent (us jaisa) circuit (kitab ki Figure 9.25 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Asal cell ko ek pure emf E aur us ke saath series mein internal resistance r samjha jata hai; dono cell ke andar hain, is liye ek hi oval (daire) mein dikhaye gaye hain.

Ab emf E aur internal resistance r wale cell ka kaam dekhein (Fig. 9.26). Infinite (bohat zyada) resistance wala voltmeter bahar wali resistance R par potential difference naapta hai, jo cell ke terminals ka potential difference V bhi hai. Circuit mein current:

blocks.alt: Oopar ki taar mein cell (E aur r oval khaake mein); darmiyani shaakh mein voltmeter cell ke terminals ke aar paar; daen taraf switch S; neeche teer wali badalne wali resistance R.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.26: cell ka terminal potential difference V = E - Ir (kitab ki Figure 9.26 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: S khula ho to current nahi chalta aur voltmeter E padhta hai. S band karne par current I chalta hai, cell ke andar Ir volt kharch hote hain, aur voltmeter V = E − Ir padhta hai.

Yahan IR = V current I ki presence (maujoodgi) mein cell ka terminal potential difference hai. Jab switch S khula ho to resistance se koi current nahi guzarta; tab voltmeter terminal voltage ke taur par emf E hi padhta hai. Is liye current chalne par (switch ON) terminal voltage emf E se Ir kam hota hai.

blocks.title: Kya aap jaante hain? (Do You Know?)
blocks.text: Cell ke terminals par laga voltmeter (a) khule circuit (open circuit) par cell ka emf naapta hai, (b) band circuit (closed circuit) par terminal potential difference naapta hai.

blocks.alt: Do circuits. (a) Cell E aur us ke aar paar sirf voltmeter (surkh taarein). (b) Cell E resistance R se juda, aur voltmeter cell ke terminals ke aar paar (neeli taarein).
blocks.caption: Do You Know? (PDF page 214): cell ke terminals ke aar paar voltmeter (a) khule circuit par cell ki emf, (b) band circuit par terminal potential difference napta hai (kitab ke is box ki tasveer ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Eq. 9.42 ko energy ke hisaab se samjhein. Baen taraf cell ka emf E hai: woh energy jo unit charge cell ke negative (manfi) terminal se positive terminal tak jate hue hasil karta hai. Daen taraf batata hai ke yeh energy circuit mein kahan kharch hoti hai: unit charge ke guzarne par Ir ke barabar energy cell ke andar kharch hoti hai, aur baqi energy bahar wali resistance R mein, jo potential drop IR hai. Yani emf batata hai ke cell har unit charge ko kitni energy deta hai, aur mukhtalif hisson par potential drops batate hain ke yeh energy kahan doosri shaklon (maslan heat) mein badli.

emf “cause” (wajah) hai aur potential difference us ka “effect” (asar). emf hamesha maujood rehta hai chahe cell se current na liya jaye, lekin kisi conductor par potential difference tab zero hota hai jab us mein current na behe.

blocks.title: Example 9.9
blocks.problem: Khule circuit mein battery ke terminals ka potential difference 2.2 V hai. 5.0 Ω resistance se jorne par yeh gir kar 1.8 V ho jata hai. Current aur battery ki internal resistance nikalein.
steps: Diya gaya: E = 2.2 V (khule circuit wali reading = emf), R = 5.0 Ω, V = 1.8 V
Current: V = IR se I = V/R = 1.8 V/5.0 Ω = 0.36 A
Internal resistance: E = V + Ir, yani 2.2 V = 1.8 V + 0.36 A × r
blocks.answer: I = 0.36 A aur r = 1.1 V A⁻¹ = 1.1 Ω

blocks.prompt: Battery se zyada current lene par us ka terminal potential difference kyun kam ho jata hai (constructed response 9.6)? 0.2 Ω internal resistance wali 12 V battery 3.6 Ω resistor se jori hai; terminal voltage nikalein (numerical 9.10).
blocks.explanation: V = E − Ir: internal resistance par voltage ka girna (Ir) current ke saath barhta hai, is liye terminals par emf ka kam hissa bachta hai. I = E/(R + r) = 12 V/3.8 Ω = 3.16 A, aur V = IR = 3.16 A × 3.6 Ω = 11.4 V.

items: emf E = W/Q (9.41): source ki har unit charge ko di gayi energy, unit volt; cell mein chemical energy se aati hai.
Electrolyte ki wajah se internal resistance r: I = E/(R + r), E = IR + Ir (9.42); terminal voltage V = E − Ir; khule circuit par V = E.
emf cause, potential difference effect. Example 9.9: I = 0.36 A, r = 1.1 Ω.
